topics.title: Purpose and Overview of the Five-Step Process

segments.content: Open with the purpose before the mechanics of the five-step revenue recognition model. Revenue should depict the transfer of promised goods or services for the consideration the company expects to receive. Preview that the five steps work as one connected chain, not five separate rules. Airbus agreeing to sell airplanes to Cathay Pacific for 100 million euros is the running example that carries through every step ahead.
must_say: Revenue should depict the transfer of promised goods or services for the consideration the company expects to receive.

beats.anchor: the five-step revenue recognition model
revenue should depict the transfer of promised goods or services

payload.text: Revenue depicts the transfer of promised goods or services for expected consideration

beats.anchor: Airbus agreeing to sell airplanes to Cathay Pacific for 100 million euros

payload.text: Running example: Airbus sells airplanes to Cathay Pacific for €100 million

segments.content: Show the five steps as one connected chain rather than an isolated checklist: identify the contract, identify performance obligations, determine the transaction price, allocate the transaction price, and recognize revenue. Each link depends on the one before it, so skipping ahead breaks the chain and costs marks.

beats.anchor: identify the contract, identify performance obligations, determine the transaction price, allocate the transaction price, and recognize revenue
each link depends on the one before it

payload.text: Each link depends on the one before it

segments.content: Walk the Airbus example through each link so the chain feels concrete rather than abstract. Identifying the customer contract is the Airbus-Cathay Pacific agreement itself. Identifying performance obligations means airplane delivery is the one promise in this basic example. Determining the transaction price means the agreement fixes it at 100 million euros. Allocating the transaction price gives the single obligation the full 100 million, because there is only one promise to satisfy. Recognizing revenue when the obligation is satisfied means revenue is recorded only once delivery transfers control of the airplanes to Cathay Pacific.

payload.text: Step 2 — Obligation: deliver the airplanes

beats.anchor: determining the transaction price means the agreement fixes it at 100 million euros

payload.text: Step 3 — Price: fixed at €100 million

beats.anchor: allocating the transaction price gives the single obligation the full 100 million

payload.text: Step 4 — Allocation: full €100 million to one obligation

beats.anchor: recognizing revenue only once delivery transfers control of the airplanes

payload.text: Step 5 — Recognition: booked at delivery

segments.content: Close by stressing that this sequence prevents recognition before the company has identified, measured, and satisfied its promise. Say the exam-strategy line once before asking the question.

beats.anchor: what loses you marks in the five-step model

payload.text: Treating the five steps as separate rules instead of one chain that ends only when the obligation is satisfied.

assessment.question: In the five-step model, what determines when a company actually records revenue?
assessment.expected_answer: Revenue is recorded only once the performance obligation is satisfied and control of the promised good or service has transferred, not simply once the contract is signed or the price is set.

options.text: As soon as the customer signs the contract
Only once the performance obligation is satisfied and control transfers
As soon as the transaction price has been determined

assessment.reexplain_guide: Use a simple sale: confirm the agreement, identify what was promised, determine and allocate the price, then record revenue only when the promise is fulfilled.

beats.anchor: what determines when a company actually records revenue

payload.stem: What determines when a company actually records revenue?

options.text: Signing the contract
Obligation satisfied, control transferred
Transaction price determined

topics.loses_marks: Treating the five steps as separate rules instead of one chain that ends only when the obligation is satisfied.

remediation.content: Re-anchor on the chain already on the board: contract, obligations, price, allocation, recognition. Recognition is last for a reason.
Use one analogy from outside accounting: agreeing to rent an apartment is not the same as moving in and getting the keys. Signing starts the chain; it does not finish it.

beats.anchor: signing the lease is not the same as getting the keys

payload.text: Signing starts the chain, not the finish

remediation.content: Re-anchor on the chain: the price is only step three. Two more links, allocation and recognition, still have to happen before revenue is recorded.

topics.title: Step 1: Identify the Contract with Customers

segments.content: Teach the contract criteria as a decision gate, not an isolated list. Five conditions must all be true before a qualifying contract exists. The parties must approve the arrangement and commit to perform their obligations. The arrangement must have commercial substance, not merely paperwork. Each party's rights to the goods or services must be identifiable, and so must the payment terms. Finally, the company must conclude that collecting the consideration is probable. Contracts may be written, oral, or implied, but revenue is not recognized until every condition is met and performance occurs. Name each criterion as you reach it.

payload.text: Approved by both parties, who commit to perform

beats.anchor: the arrangement must have commercial substance

payload.text: Has commercial substance, not just paperwork

payload.text: Each party's rights are identifiable

beats.anchor: the payment terms must be identifiable too

payload.text: Payment terms are identifiable

beats.anchor: the company must conclude that collecting the consideration is probable

payload.text: Collection of consideration is probable

segments.content: Contrast a qualifying contract with a wholly unperformed arrangement that either party can terminate without compensation, so the student sees why an approved agreement alone is not enough.

assessment.question: Which of these arrangements satisfies the criteria for a qualifying contract?
assessment.expected_answer: A firm, approved order with identifiable rights, clear payment terms, and probable collection satisfies the criteria; an unenforceable or still-negotiated arrangement does not.

topics.title: Step 2: Identify Separate Performance Obligations

segments.content: Focus on the meaning of a distinct promise and the effect of interdependence. A performance obligation is a promise to transfer a distinct good or service, and the customer must be able to benefit from it on its own. Finish with the three-part test: identify each promise, decide whether it is distinct, and determine whether it is independent or part of one integrated output.
must_say: A performance obligation is a promise to transfer a distinct good or service, and the customer must be able to benefit from it.

beats.anchor: a performance obligation is a promise to transfer a distinct good or service
the customer must be able to benefit from it on its own

chunks: A performance obligation is a promise
to transfer a distinct good or service
that the customer can benefit from on its own

beats.anchor: identify each promise, decide whether it is distinct, and check independence

payload.text: Test: identify, check distinct, check independent

segments.content: Use SoftTech to show that two promises can form a single integrated obligation. SoftTech licenses software and performs extensive customization so significant that neither promise is separable from the other. Because the two are interdependent, they are accounted for as one performance obligation, not two.

beats.anchor: SoftTech licenses software and performs extensive customization

payload.text: SoftTech: license + customization = one integrated obligation

beats.anchor: the two are interdependent, so they are one performance obligation

payload.text: Interdependent promises combine into a single obligation

segments.content: Contrast that with Chen Computer, which sells a laptop with a standard assurance warranty and offers an optional extended service warranty. The assurance warranty simply supports the laptop working as promised, so it stays bundled with that obligation. The extended warranty can be bought or declined on its own, which is exactly what makes it a second, independent performance obligation.

beats.anchor: the assurance warranty stays bundled while the extended warranty is independent

rows.x: No, part of the laptop obligation

beats.anchor: buyable separately is exactly what makes it a distinct obligation

payload.text: Buyable separately = separate obligation

segments.content: Say the exam-strategy line once before asking the question.

beats.anchor: what loses you marks on performance obligations

payload.text: Counting one integrated output as two obligations, or missing a genuinely separate one like an optional extended warranty.

assessment.question: Chen Computer sells a laptop with a standard assurance warranty and offers an optional extended service warranty. How many performance obligations exist if the customer buys both?
assessment.expected_answer: Two: the laptop with its assurance warranty is one obligation, and the separately purchasable extended service warranty is a second, independent obligation.

options.text: Two: the laptop with its assurance warranty, and the extended warranty
One: warranties are never separate from the product
Three: the laptop, the assurance warranty, and the extended warranty

assessment.reexplain_guide: Use a computer example: an assurance warranty supports the computer and stays with that obligation, while an optional extended service warranty can be purchased separately and is its own obligation.

beats.anchor: how many performance obligations exist for the laptop and both warranties

payload.stem: How many performance obligations exist if the customer buys both warranties?

options.text: Two: laptop+assurance, and extended warranty
One: warranties never separate
Three: laptop, assurance, extended

topics.loses_marks: Counting one integrated output as two obligations, or missing a genuinely separate one like an optional extended warranty.

remediation.content: Re-anchor on the definition already on the board: distinct, and the customer can benefit from it on its own.
Contrast the two warranties directly: the assurance warranty cannot be bought or declined on its own, but the extended warranty can, which is exactly what makes it distinct.

beats.anchor: a warranty the customer can buy separately is a separate obligation

payload.text: Buyable separately = separate obligation

remediation.content: Point back at the assurance warranty specifically: it cannot be purchased or declined on its own, so it is not a distinct promise, it travels with the laptop.

beats.anchor: the assurance warranty cannot be purchased or declined on its own

payload.text: Not separately purchasable = not a distinct promise

topics.title: Step 3: Determine the Transaction Price

segments.content: Explain transaction price as the consideration the company expects in exchange for transferring goods or services. It is not simply the invoice price: fixed consideration is only the starting point. Introduce variable consideration next, the amounts that depend on discounts, rebates, performance bonuses, or royalties.

beats.anchor: the transaction price is the consideration the company expects in exchange
fixed consideration is only the starting point

payload.text: Fixed consideration is the starting point, not the total

beats.anchor: variable consideration depends on discounts, rebates, bonuses, or royalties

segments.content: Beyond the basic price, watch for three adjustments the exam likes to test. A significant financing component separates true sales revenue from interest income. Non-cash consideration, such as equity or goods received in exchange, is generally measured at fair value. Payments a company makes to its customer, like a rebate check, usually reduce the transaction price rather than count as a marketing expense.

beats.anchor: a significant financing component separates sales revenue from interest

payload.text: Significant financing separates revenue from interest

beats.anchor: non-cash consideration is generally measured at fair value

payload.text: Non-cash consideration measured at fair value

beats.anchor: payments to customers usually reduce revenue

payload.text: Payments to the customer usually reduce revenue

segments.content: Contrast probability-weighted expected value with the single most likely amount as the two ways to estimate variable consideration. Use Peabody briefly: the probability-weighted estimate is 147,500 dollars, while the single most likely outcome is 150,000 dollars.

beats.anchor: two ways to estimate variable consideration

payload.text: Two methods: expected value, or most likely amount

beats.anchor: expected value weighs every outcome, most likely amount picks one

rows.x: Weights every possible outcome by its probability
rows.y: Picks the single most probable outcome

segments.content: Say the exam-strategy line once before asking the question.

beats.anchor: what loses you marks estimating the transaction price

payload.text: Using the most likely amount for a wide range of possible outcomes instead of the probability-weighted expected value.

assessment.question: A contract has many possible variable-consideration outcomes spread across a wide range. Which estimation method should the company use?
assessment.expected_answer: The probability-weighted expected value, because it accounts for the full range of possible outcomes rather than only the single most probable one.

options.text: Probability-weighted expected value across all outcomes
Always the single most likely outcome, regardless of the range
The fixed contract price only, ignoring variable amounts

assessment.reexplain_guide: Describe expected value as averaging all outcomes using their probabilities, while most likely amount chooses the one outcome with the highest probability.

beats.anchor: which estimation method fits a wide range of outcomes

payload.stem: Which estimation method fits a wide range of possible outcomes?

options.text: Probability-weighted expected value
Always the single most likely outcome
Fixed price only, ignore variable amounts

topics.loses_marks: Using the most likely amount for a wide range of possible outcomes instead of the probability-weighted expected value.

remediation.content: Re-anchor on the Peabody numbers already on the board: 147,500 versus 150,000, and why they differ.
Point out that most likely amount only fits when there are few possible outcomes clustered close together; a wide spread needs expected value instead.

beats.anchor: a wide spread of outcomes needs expected value, not one guess

payload.text: Wide spread needs expected value

remediation.content: Return to the definition: transaction price includes variable consideration such as discounts, rebates, bonuses, and royalties, not only the fixed amount on the invoice.

beats.anchor: transaction price includes variable consideration, not only the fixed amount

payload.text: Transaction price includes variable consideration too

topics.title: Step 4: Allocate the Transaction Price

segments.content: Explain allocation using relative standalone selling prices, and work one example fully. Standalone prices of 80 and 20 add up to a total of 100. That ratio is eighty percent and twenty percent. A transaction price of 90 is split the same way: eighty percent of 90 is 72, and twenty percent of 90 is 18. Say every step out loud in order and leave the example visible as the model.

beats.anchor: standalone prices of 80 and 20 add up to a total of 100

payload.text: Total standalone value: 80 + 20 = 100

beats.anchor: the split is eighty percent and twenty percent of the standalone prices
eighty percent of 90 is 72
twenty percent of 90 is 18

segments.content: An observable separate selling price is the best evidence and needs no estimate. When prices are unavailable, three approaches step in: adjusted market assessment asks what the market would pay, expected cost plus a margin builds the price up from cost, and the residual approach subtracts known prices from the bundle total. Allocation is needed only when a contract contains more than one performance obligation.

beats.anchor: an observable separate selling price is the best evidence

payload.text: Observable standalone price is the best evidence

beats.anchor: when no observable price exists use adjusted market, cost-plus-margin, or the residual approach

payload.text: Adjusted market, cost-plus-margin, or residual approach

beats.anchor: allocation is needed only when a contract contains more than one performance obligation

payload.text: Only needed with more than one obligation

segments.content: Now run the same procedure with the final numbers hidden. Give a second bundle: standalone prices of 90 and 60, transaction price of 120. Ask the student to supply the ratio and the allocated amount for the higher-priced item, using the same three steps just demonstrated in the worked example, which stays visible as the model.

assessment.question: A bundle sells for 200 SAR. The standalone selling prices of the two components are 150 SAR and 50 SAR. How much of the 200 SAR is allocated to the first component?
assessment.expected_answer: 150 SAR, because 150 over the total standalone value of 200 is seventy-five percent, and seventy-five percent of the 200 SAR transaction price is 150 SAR.
assessment.reexplain_guide: Use a 100-dollar bundle containing items normally sold for 75 dollars and 25 dollars. Their relative values allocate 75 dollars and 25 dollars.

topics.title: Step 5: Recognize Revenue When the Obligation Is Satisfied

segments.content: Center the explanation on transfer of control. Satisfying the performance obligation triggers recognition, not merely signing the contract or sending an invoice. Return to Airbus: the contract signed in March creates no revenue by itself. Delivery in June transfers control and triggers recognition of the full 100 million euros.

payload.text: Signing or billing does not trigger recognition

beats.anchor: delivery in June transfers control and triggers recognition

payload.text: Airbus: revenue recognized in June at delivery, not March at signing

segments.content: For point-in-time recognition, discuss indicators such as rights to payment, legal title, physical possession, risks and rewards, and customer acceptance. For over-time recognition, explain that revenue follows progress as control transfers continuously, using measures such as cost-to-cost and units delivered. Match the pattern to how control actually transfers.

topics.title: Apply the Complete Five-Step Process

segments.content: Synthesize the model as a decision chain rather than reteaching every detail. Connect Steps 1 and 2 as establishing the accounting unit through the contract and distinct promises. Connect Steps 3 and 4 as measuring the expected consideration and assigning it to obligations. Connect Step 5 to recording revenue as control transfers.

segments.content: Apply the whole chain to Airbus one more time, stage by stage. Steps one and two together give a qualifying contract with Cathay Pacific and one performance obligation to deliver the airplanes. Step three fixes the transaction price at 100 million euros. Step four allocates the full amount to that single obligation, since there is only one promise. Step five recognizes revenue only once delivery transfers control, in June. Stress that skipping any stage breaks the chain and costs the mark.
